case.title: The Last Séance
case.central_mystery: Five college friends held one last reunion at abandoned Blackwood Manor before life pulled them apart. During a Ouija board session, the board spelled a single word — LIAR — moments before the manor lost power. When the lights came back, Jake Whitfield was dead by the fireplace, struck once with an iron poker. Everyone swears nobody moved in the dark.
case.why_no_direct_evidence_exists: The blackout lasted under two minutes, was genuinely unplanned by the killer, and covered the only window in which the murder could have occurred. No camera exists inside the manor. Every other piece of the truth is buried in a three-year-old cover-up none of the friends have ever discussed outside their own circle.

weather.general_pattern: Cold, clear autumn night, no storm. Full moon obscured by high cloud after 10 PM.
weather.relevance_to_case: Clear weather rules out a storm-caused power outage, making the manor's blackout suspicious in isolation until it is traced to a genuinely mundane cause: a groundskeeper working on a failing fuse box.

victim.name: Jake Whitfield
victim.physical_description: Tall, lean, prematurely tired-looking for his age. Wore a plain silver ring he never explained.
victim.personality: Warm but increasingly withdrawn over the past year. The one who kept the friend group together for years; lately the one pulling away from it.
victim.current_project: Had been quietly seeing a therapist for eight months and had recently decided to go to the police about an incident from three years ago.
victim.last_seen_alive: Seated at the seance table in the manor's drawing room, seconds before the power failed.
victim.missing_items: None. His phone, wallet, and belongings were untouched.

suspects.name: Leo Bennett
suspects.role: Medical student, engaged to be married in the spring
suspects.relationship_to_victim: One of Jake's four closest friends since freshman year
suspects.personality: Controlled, articulate, the group's natural leader. Good at staying calm, almost too good, under pressure.
suspects.motive_on_paper: None visible. No known conflict with Jake; by all accounts they were close.
suspects.secret: Killed Jake in the blackout to prevent him from confessing to a hit-and-run the five of them covered up three years ago, which would end Leo's medical career and engagement.
suspects.alibi_claim: Says he was seated directly across the seance table from Jake the entire time, and ran toward the sound of Jake falling the instant the lights returned.
suspects.alibi_evidence: No one can confirm exact positions in the dark, which is precisely why his claim has never been challenged directly.

suspects.name: Sam Ostrowski
suspects.role: IT support technician, amateur electronics hobbyist
suspects.relationship_to_victim: Longtime friend, known for pranks and elaborate jokes
suspects.personality: Nervous energy, over-explains things when anxious, genuinely liked by the group.
suspects.motive_on_paper: None for murder. Has an obvious, embarrassing reason to lie about the seance itself.
suspects.secret: Rigged the Ouija board with a hidden wireless vibration motor as a prank. After Jake's death, panicked that he'd be blamed for planning a murder, and secretly removed the device from under the table and hid it in Priya's backpack.
suspects.alibi_claim: Claims he never touched the board and has no idea how it moved.
suspects.alibi_evidence: Denies everything about the device until confronted with purchase and forum evidence.

suspects.name: Priya Anand
suspects.personality: Precise, guarded, visibly the most anxious of the group even before the murder.
suspects.motive_on_paper: The rigging device was found in her bag, making her the apparent architect of the seance's fear campaign, and by extension, a suspect in staging conditions for murder.
suspects.secret: Was in the car the night of the hit-and-run three years ago and has been secretly sending money to the victim's family ever since, without telling the others.
suspects.alibi_claim: Says she has no idea how the device got into her bag and was nowhere near the table when the lights went out.
suspects.alibi_evidence: Her bag was on the floor near the room's entrance, several feet from the table, physically awkward for her to have planted anything under it herself.

suspects.name: Mia Torres
suspects.role: Recently engaged, works in event planning
suspects.personality: Warm in public, sharp and controlling in private moments; the most emotionally invested in the group's silence staying intact.
suspects.motive_on_paper: Had a heated, witnessed argument with Jake the day before his death, begging him not to go to the police.
suspects.secret: Genuinely tried to talk Jake out of confessing, out of fear for her own upcoming wedding and reputation, but did not kill him.
suspects.alibi_claim: Says she was standing near Leo throughout the blackout.
suspects.alibi_evidence: True, but her presence near Leo is exactly why no one thought to separate their accounts.

suspects.name: Daniel Reyes
suspects.role: Part-time caretaker of the Blackwood estate grounds
suspects.relationship_to_victim: Younger brother of Elena Reyes, killed in the hit-and-run three years ago. Secretly contacted by Jake weeks before his death.
suspects.personality: Quiet, guarded around outsiders, carries old grief without performing it.
suspects.motive_on_paper: Once the hit-and-run is uncovered, has the single clearest revenge motive of anyone in the case, plus keys and legitimate access to the manor.
suspects.secret: Was on the grounds that night repairing a failing fuse box, the real, mundane cause of the blackout, and had already privately forgiven Jake after receiving his apology.
suspects.alibi_claim: Says he was in the manor's old cellar junction box the entire evening and never entered the drawing room.
suspects.alibi_evidence: No one saw him there directly, since the seance group assumed the manor was empty aside from themselves.

witnesses.name: Ruth Calloway
witnesses.role: Night clerk, Millhaven Fuel and Grocery
witnesses.statement: Recognized Leo's blue sedan passing the station twice that night, once around 7:40 PM alone, and again near 9:15 PM with the full group.
witnesses.truthfulness: Fully truthful, has no reason to lie.
witnesses.reliability: High, station till receipts corroborate her timeline independently.

witnesses.name: Denise Okafor
witnesses.statement: Overheard Mia and Jake arguing in a booth the afternoon before his death, Mia crying, saying 'you'll ruin everything,' Jake calm and apologetic.
witnesses.truthfulness: Truthful, recalls it clearly because it was unusually tense for the group.

witnesses.name: Frank Doyle
witnesses.statement: Leo came in alone around 8 PM, ordered a drink he barely touched, checked his phone repeatedly, and left after twenty minutes looking unsettled.
witnesses.reliability: Medium-high, exact time is an estimate, not a till timestamp.

witnesses.name: Helen Reyes
witnesses.statement: Confirms she has received anonymous money transfers for two years, always memo'd only with a small flower emoji, and confirms Daniel had no plan to confront anyone, he told her he'd already 'let it go' after a recent call from one of Elena's old friends.
witnesses.truthfulness: Fully truthful, speaks with quiet grief rather than anger.

vehicles.relevant_movement: Passed Millhaven Fuel and Grocery alone at 7:40 PM, nearly two hours before the group's agreed 9:00 PM arrival time, then again with the group at 9:15 PM.
Left Mia's apartment at 8:50 PM carrying Mia, Sam, Priya, and Jake; arrived at the manor gate at 9:12 PM.

cctv.footage: Leo's sedan pulls in alone, he buys nothing, sits in the car for six minutes, then drives off toward the manor road rather than back toward town.
cctv.status: Recovered, timestamp verified against station register.

cctv.footage: Same sedan passes again, now with four visible passengers, consistent with the group's stated arrival time.
Leo alone at the bar, visibly checking his phone repeatedly.
cctv.status: Recovered, low resolution but timestamp intact.

phone_calls.content_summary: Phone company records confirm the call occurred; content unknown, but this is the call in which Jake privately told Leo he intended to go to the police that Monday.

messages.text: I know this changes everything for you especially. I'm still doing it Monday. I just needed you to hear it from me first.
Please don't do this. You're not the only one this destroys.
I've carried it for three years, Mia. I can't anymore. I'm not naming anyone who doesn't want to be named.

bank_records.transaction: Recurring transfer to Helen Reyes, memo: small flower emoji only
bank_records.purpose_established: Anonymous guilt payments following the hit-and-run three years ago.
bank_records.relevance: Confirms Priya's presence in the cover-up and ongoing guilt, unrelated to the murder itself, a red herring for the murder but real evidence toward the hit-and-run.

locations.name: The Drawing Room (Seance Room)
locations.description: Where the seance and murder took place. Circular table at the center, an old stone fireplace with an iron poker set along the east wall.
locations.repeat_search_changes: A second search with better lighting reveals a faint drag mark near the fireplace inconsistent with a fall.

locations.name: Manor Study
locations.description: Small side room where Mia and Leo claim to have been standing during the blackout.
possible_tests: dust disturbance analysis on the floor

locations.name: Manor Cellar and Fuse Room
locations.description: Where Daniel Reyes was working on the failing electrical panel the night of the murder.
possible_tests: timestamp check on the fuse box repair log

locations.name: Manor Grounds and Driveway
locations.description: The gravel approach to the manor, gate, and tree line.
searchable_objects: gate log book kept by caretaker

locations.name: Millhaven Fuel and Grocery
locations.description: Gas station on the road between town and the manor.

locations.name: The Copper Kettle Diner
locations.description: Where Mia and Jake argued the day before his death.

locations.name: Frank's Tavern
locations.description: Where Leo stopped alone before the manor gathering.

locations.name: Reyes Family Home
locations.description: Helen Reyes' home, where Daniel lives.
searchable_objects: a small memorial shelf for Elena

blackwood_manor.access_summary: Single main entrance, one side door near the kitchen usually locked from outside, cellar accessible via a hatch in the kitchen floor.

crime_scene.location: The Drawing Room, beside the fireplace
crime_scene.condition_on_discovery: Jake found face-down near the hearth, seance circle broken, candles knocked over but not burning anything.
crime_scene.initial_assumption: A fall in the dark during panic when the lights failed.
crime_scene.actual_nature: A single deliberate strike to the back of the skull with the fireplace poker, delivered during the blackout, then staged to look like Jake had simply fallen and struck his head.
crime_scene.key_scene_contradiction: The wound pattern is inconsistent with a fall, a fall would strike the front or side of the skull as a person stumbles forward, not the precise rear strike found here.

autopsy.cause_of_death: Single blunt force trauma to the occipital region of the skull
additional_findings: No defensive wounds, Jake did not see the strike coming
No signs of a struggle beforehand
Death would have been rapid, within a minute or two of the blow
autopsy.conclusion: Homicide, not an accidental fall. The strike required precision inconsistent with panic or random stumbling in the dark.

forensics.finding: Wiped clean of prints, but one partial print recovered near the handle's base, consistent with Leo Bennett's right hand once compared against a voluntarily provided sample.
forensics.plausibility_note: Leo's explanation, that he touched the poker earlier in the evening while adding wood to the fire, is plausible on its own, which is why this alone isn't conclusive without the timeline evidence.

forensics.finding: A small wireless vibration motor with a phone-paired remote trigger, recovered from Priya's backpack. Fingerprint analysis shows Sam Ostrowski's prints on the device's internals, with only smudged, non-matching prints on the bag's exterior zipper.
forensics.plausibility_note: The device's internal prints prove who built and operated it; the mismatch on the bag proves it was placed there by someone other than its owner.

forensics.finding: Trace soil matching the manor's gravel driveway found in the tread, in a pattern consistent with two separate visits rather than one.
forensics.plausibility_note: Consistent with the gas station footage showing him passing the manor road nearly two hours before the group's arrival.

evidence.name: Seance Table Underside Residue
evidence.description: Faint adhesive residue on the underside of the table, consistent with tape once used to mount something.
evidence.required_action: Examine the seance table closely.
evidence.why_it_exists: Physical remnant of Sam's original taping of the device before he removed it.

evidence.name: Vibration Motor Device
evidence.description: A small wireless-triggered vibration motor with a paired remote app, found zipped inside Priya's backpack.
evidence.required_action: Search bags left in the drawing room.
evidence.why_it_exists: The physical object at the center of the seance mystery, planted evidence Sam moved after the murder.

evidence.name: Device Internal Fingerprints
evidence.description: Forensic analysis of the device's internal components shows fingerprints matching Sam Ostrowski.
evidence.required_action: Request forensic fingerprint analysis on the recovered device.
evidence.why_it_exists: Proves Sam built and operated the device, regardless of where it was found.

evidence.name: Bag Zipper Print Mismatch
evidence.description: The zipper pull of Priya's bag shows only smudged prints inconsistent with a clean plant by its owner.
evidence.required_action: Request forensic analysis of the bag's exterior.
evidence.why_it_exists: Suggests the device was placed into the bag by someone else, after the fact.

evidence.name: Online Hobbyist Forum Post
evidence.description: A post under Sam's known username, three months prior, asking about wireless vibration motors small enough to hide under a table for a prank.
evidence.required_action: Request a records check on Sam's known online accounts.
evidence.why_it_exists: Establishes premeditation of the prank, unrelated to any murder plan.

evidence.name: Gas Station Till Log, 19:40
evidence.description: Register timestamp showing no purchase, but a car matching Leo's plate idling at pump 3.
evidence.required_action: Request the gas station's till and camera records.
evidence.why_it_exists: First hard evidence Leo was near the manor far earlier than he claims.

evidence.name: Gas Station CCTV, 19:35-19:45
evidence.description: Footage of Leo's sedan passing alone, sitting briefly, then continuing toward the manor road.
evidence.required_action: Request CCTV footage from the station.
evidence.why_it_exists: Visual confirmation of Leo's early, unexplained presence near the manor.

evidence.name: Tavern Tab Receipt
evidence.description: A single drink, mostly untouched, paid by card under Leo's name at 8:04 PM.
evidence.required_action: Request receipts from Frank's Tavern.
evidence.why_it_exists: Corroborates the timeline of Leo's anxious solo movements before the reunion.

evidence.name: Gate Log Book Entry
evidence.description: Daniel's handwritten caretaker log shows an entry for recurring fuse box fault logged earlier that week.
evidence.required_action: Search the manor grounds for caretaker records.
evidence.why_it_exists: Establishes the fuse box problem was real and pre-existing, not staged.

evidence.name: Tire Tread Near Gate
evidence.description: A second, earlier set of tire impressions near the gate distinct from the group's later arrival tracks.
evidence.required_action: Request a tread comparison of vehicle tracks at the gate.
evidence.why_it_exists: Physical corroboration of Leo's early visit to the property.

evidence.name: Jake's Therapy Appointment Log
evidence.description: Confirms eight months of regular sessions; content is privileged, but the pattern of increasing frequency in the final month is on record.
evidence.required_action: Request Jake's appointment records with next of kin consent.
evidence.why_it_exists: Establishes Jake's psychological state and timeline of building toward a decision.

evidence.name: Jake's Personal Journal
evidence.description: A journal entry dated one week before his death: I've decided. Monday. I owe her that much, even if it costs me everyone else.
evidence.required_action: Search Jake's belongings.
evidence.why_it_exists: Direct evidence of Jake's decision to confess, and the timeline it was made on.

evidence.name: Text Message: Jake to Leo, Oct 16
evidence.description: I know this changes everything for you especially. I'm still doing it Monday. I just needed you to hear it from me first.
evidence.required_action: Request Jake's phone message records.
evidence.why_it_exists: Direct proof Leo specifically knew and had the strongest personal stake in stopping it.

evidence.name: Poker Partial Print
evidence.description: A partial print near the poker's handle base, not fully wiped.
evidence.required_action: Request forensic analysis of the fireplace poker.
evidence.why_it_exists: Physical link between the murder weapon and its user.

evidence.name: Fireplace Ash Disturbance
evidence.description: Ash swept slightly, as if something was quickly wiped near the hearth.
evidence.required_action: Examine the fireplace area closely.
evidence.why_it_exists: Physical trace of the killer wiping the weapon in a hurry.

evidence.name: Autopsy Report
evidence.description: Confirms a single rear skull strike, no defensive wounds, death within the blackout window.
evidence.required_action: Request the autopsy findings.
evidence.why_it_exists: Establishes the medical reality contradicting the accidental fall assumption.

evidence.name: Wound Angle Analysis
evidence.description: The strike angle is inconsistent with a forward fall onto the hearth.
evidence.required_action: Request a forensic wound-angle consultation.
evidence.why_it_exists: Rules out the he simply fell theory conclusively.

evidence.name: Diner Staff Statement
evidence.description: Denise Okafor recalls Mia crying and saying you'll ruin everything to Jake the day before his death.
evidence.required_action: Interview diner staff about the day before the incident.
evidence.why_it_exists: Establishes Mia's motive on paper, a genuine red herring.

evidence.name: Text Message: Mia to Jake, Oct 17
evidence.description: Please don't do this. You're not the only one this destroys.
evidence.required_action: Request Jake's phone message records.
evidence.why_it_exists: Direct written confirmation of Mia's desperation, deepening suspicion of her before it's cleared.

evidence.name: Text Message: Jake to Mia, Oct 17
evidence.description: I've carried it for three years, Mia. I can't anymore. I'm not naming anyone who doesn't want to be named.
evidence.required_action: Request Jake's phone message records.
evidence.why_it_exists: Shows Jake intended a measured, protective confession, undercutting any theory that he was about to name Mia specifically.

evidence.name: Mia's Own Alibi Statement
evidence.description: Mia states she was standing beside Leo the entire blackout.
evidence.required_action: Interview Mia about her position during the blackout.
evidence.why_it_exists: True, but incidentally shields Leo rather than incriminating her.

evidence.name: Study Room Dust Disturbance
evidence.description: Floor dust in the study shows two sets of stationary footprints, consistent with two people standing still.
evidence.required_action: Examine the study floor.
evidence.why_it_exists: Physical corroboration that Mia genuinely didn't move, narrowing suspicion away from her.

evidence.name: Old Police Report, 2022 Hit-and-Run
evidence.description: Unsolved case file: Elena Reyes, 26, struck and killed by an unidentified vehicle, no arrests made.
evidence.required_action: Request archived police records for unsolved cases three years prior.
evidence.why_it_exists: The root event the entire case pivots on.

evidence.name: Elena Reyes Obituary
evidence.description: Local newspaper obituary, confirms date and circumstances.
evidence.required_action: Search local newspaper archives.
evidence.why_it_exists: Corroborates the timeline and identity of the victim from three years ago.

evidence.name: Body Shop Repair Receipt
evidence.description: A receipt for front bumper and headlight repair on a vehicle registered to Leo Bennett's family, dated two days after Elena's death.
evidence.required_action: Request vehicle repair records around the date of the old hit-and-run.
evidence.why_it_exists: Direct physical link between the friend group's vehicle and the original crime.

evidence.name: Group Chat Fragment (Recovered)
evidence.description: A partially recovered deleted message thread from three years ago: We never talk about tonight again. Ever. Sent to all five friends.
evidence.required_action: Request phone forensic recovery on old deleted messages, with consent or warrant.
evidence.why_it_exists: Direct proof of the five-way pact and cover-up.

evidence.name: Insurance Claim Inconsistency
evidence.description: The claim filed for the vehicle repair describes a deer strike, inconsistent with the body shop's internal damage assessment notes.
evidence.required_action: Cross-reference the insurance claim with body shop records.
evidence.why_it_exists: Shows deliberate falsification to hide the true cause of the damage.

evidence.name: Priya's Bank Transfer Records
evidence.description: Recurring $200 monthly transfers to Helen Reyes for two years, memo'd only with a flower emoji.
evidence.required_action: Request Priya's financial records with a warrant.
evidence.why_it_exists: Confirms Priya's guilt and involvement in the old cover-up, separate from the murder.

evidence.name: Helen Reyes' Witness Statement
evidence.description: Confirms the anonymous payments and states Daniel had already let it go recently after a call from one of Elena's old friends.
evidence.required_action: Interview Helen Reyes.
evidence.why_it_exists: Both confirms Priya's payments and clears Daniel of any active revenge motive.

evidence.name: Jake's Voicemail to Daniel Reyes
evidence.description: A voicemail, saved by Daniel, in which Jake privately apologizes and says he intends to make it right through the police, the real way, not just money.
evidence.required_action: Ask Daniel directly whether Jake ever contacted him.
evidence.why_it_exists: Proves Jake reached out to the Reyes family before his death, and that Daniel had no unresolved motive left.

evidence.name: Seance Circle Position Diagram
evidence.description: A diagram reconstructed from each friend's statement showing claimed seating positions during the blackout.
evidence.required_action: Interview all four surviving friends about exactly where they were sitting.
evidence.why_it_exists: The reconstructed map is what first reveals Leo's account doesn't match the physical distance to the body.

evidence.name: Leo's Inconsistent Position Statement
evidence.description: Leo initially says he never left his chair; later says he took a step to steady himself when the lights went out.
evidence.required_action: Re-interview Leo about his exact movements.
evidence.why_it_exists: A small but real inconsistency that opens the door to further scrutiny of his alibi.

evidence.name: Leo's Shoe Soil Analysis
evidence.description: Soil in Leo's shoe tread matches the manor's gravel driveway in a layered pattern consistent with two separate visits.
evidence.required_action: Request forensic soil analysis on Leo's shoes.
evidence.why_it_exists: Physically corroborates the earlier, unexplained visit shown on gas station footage.

evidence.name: Fuse Box Repair Log
evidence.description: Daniel's handwritten log timestamps his cellar work between 8:50 PM and 10:10 PM the night of the murder.
evidence.required_action: Search the cellar fuse room.
evidence.why_it_exists: Establishes Daniel's real, mundane presence and the genuine cause of the blackout.

evidence.name: Daniel's Toolbox
evidence.description: Contains only electrical tools, no weapon, consistent with legitimate repair work.
evidence.required_action: Search the cellar for tools.
evidence.why_it_exists: Rules out Daniel's toolbox as a weapon source.

evidence.name: Manor Blackout Duration Log
evidence.description: The fuse box's internal fault recorder shows the outage lasted exactly 94 seconds.
evidence.required_action: Request the fuse box's internal diagnostic log.
evidence.why_it_exists: Establishes the precise, narrow window in which the murder had to occur.

evidence.name: Sam's Panic Text to a Friend (Not in Group)
evidence.description: Sent an hour after the murder: I did something stupid before all this happened and now I don't know what to do. It looks so much worse than it is.
evidence.required_action: Request Sam's phone message records.
evidence.why_it_exists: Shows Sam's panic and guilt over the prank and frame-up, not the murder itself.

evidence.name: Sam's Purchase Record
evidence.description: An online order three months prior for a mini wireless vibration motor kit, delivered to Sam's address.
evidence.required_action: Request Sam's online purchase history with consent or warrant.
evidence.why_it_exists: Concrete proof Sam planned the prank well before the reunion.

evidence.name: Priya's Bag Position Statement
evidence.description: Priya states her bag was left by the entrance, not near the table, when the seance began.
evidence.required_action: Interview Priya about where she left her belongings.
evidence.why_it_exists: Supports the theory that someone moved the device to her bag after the fact, rather than her having placed it there herself.

evidence.name: Corroborating Friend Statement on Bag Placement
evidence.description: Mia independently confirms Priya's bag was by the door, not the table, all evening.
evidence.required_action: Interview Mia about where everyone's belongings were left.
evidence.why_it_exists: Independent corroboration strengthens the frame-up theory over Priya's guilt.

evidence.name: Daniel's Employment Contract
evidence.description: Confirms his legitimate, longstanding role as part-time caretaker, predating any connection to the friend group's reunion booking.
evidence.required_action: Request Daniel's employment records for the estate.
evidence.why_it_exists: Establishes his presence that night was routine, not engineered.

evidence.name: Estate Booking Record
evidence.description: Shows the friend group booked the manor for the reunion two weeks prior, through a public listing, not arranged by or with Daniel.
evidence.required_action: Request the manor's rental booking history.
evidence.why_it_exists: Rules out any theory that Daniel engineered the gathering to get close to the group.

evidence.name: Jake's Draft Police Statement
evidence.description: Found saved on Jake's laptop, dated four days before his death: a full, unsent account of the hit-and-run naming himself as present and offering full cooperation.
evidence.required_action: Search Jake's laptop with consent from next of kin.
evidence.why_it_exists: Concrete proof of exactly what Jake intended to confess and when.

evidence.name: Calendar Entry: Detective, Monday 9AM
evidence.description: A calendar reminder on Jake's phone for the Monday after his death.
evidence.required_action: Examine Jake's phone calendar.
evidence.why_it_exists: Confirms the confession was imminent, not a distant hypothetical.

evidence.name: Elena's Memorial Shelf
evidence.description: A small shelf in the Reyes home with photos and a folded newspaper clipping, undisturbed and long-settled, not the shrine of someone actively planning revenge.
evidence.required_action: Examine the Reyes family home with permission.
evidence.why_it_exists: Softens and humanizes the obvious revenge suspect read on Daniel.

evidence.name: Daniel's Recent Call Log
evidence.description: Shows a call from an unlisted number nine days before Jake's death, followed by a text to his mother saying I think I can finally stop being angry about this.
evidence.required_action: Request Daniel's phone records.
evidence.why_it_exists: Corroborates that Jake's outreach genuinely resolved Daniel's anger before the murder, clearing his motive in real time, not just after the fact.

evidence.name: Candle Wax Pattern
evidence.description: Cooled wax drip patterns on the seance table are undisturbed, indicating the candles were not moved or knocked during any struggle, only after the blackout ended.
evidence.required_action: Examine the seance table's candles closely.
evidence.why_it_exists: Supports the idea that the murder was fast, silent, and required no visible struggle.

evidence.name: Group's Verbal Reactions Transcript
evidence.description: Reconstructed from each friend's memory of who said what in the dark, everyone recalls Sam's voice shouting fearfully, but no one recalls hearing Jake make any sound at all.
evidence.required_action: Interview all four friends about what they heard during the blackout.
evidence.why_it_exists: Consistent with the autopsy's finding that Jake never saw the strike coming and could not have cried out.

evidence.name: Leo's Fiancee's Statement
evidence.description: Claire, Leo's fiancee, mentions he'd been unusually stressed about an old college thing in the week before the reunion, though she didn't know details.
evidence.required_action: Interview Leo's fiancee.
evidence.why_it_exists: Independent, unwitting corroboration that Leo was carrying a specific, recent stress tied to the past.

evidence.name: Medical School Acceptance Letter
evidence.description: A conditional acceptance letter to Leo's medical program, contingent on a clean background check finalized the following month.
evidence.required_action: Search Leo's belongings or request his admissions records.
evidence.why_it_exists: Establishes exactly what Leo stood to lose if the hit-and-run came to light, the concrete stakes behind his motive.

evidence.name: Final Forensic Poker Match
evidence.description: A follow-up, more detailed print comparison confirms the partial print on the poker matches Leo Bennett to a high degree of certainty.
evidence.required_action: Request a full comparative fingerprint analysis once Leo is formally a suspect.
evidence.why_it_exists: The final, conclusive physical link needed to move from suspicion to proof.

evidence.name: Reconstructed 94-Second Timeline
evidence.description: A full second-by-second reconstruction combining the fuse log, seating diagram, and witness statements, showing Leo had the only unaccounted, physically plausible path to the fireplace and back.
evidence.required_action: Cross-reference the blackout duration log with the seating diagram and all statements.
evidence.why_it_exists: The synthesis piece, the moment all prior evidence locks into a single, provable sequence of events.

timeline.event: Elena Reyes is struck and killed by a vehicle later traced to the five friends' group; they cover it up and swear silence.
Jake begins therapy, initially for unrelated stress.
Sam orders a wireless vibration motor kit online, planning a seance prank for the upcoming reunion.
Jake privately calls Daniel Reyes and leaves a voicemail apologizing and stating his intent to go to the police.
Daniel tells his mother, Helen, that he has finally let it go.
Jake calls Leo privately and tells him he intends to confess to the police on Monday.
Mia and Jake argue by text; Mia begs him to reconsider.
Leo drives past the manor road alone, stopping briefly near the gate before continuing.
Leo stops at Frank's Tavern alone, visibly anxious, checking his phone.
Daniel Reyes begins repair work on the manor's failing fuse box, unaware anyone else is on the property yet.
The group arrives together at the manor.
The seance begins in the drawing room.
The Ouija board spells LIAR, triggered remotely by Sam.
The manor's power fails for 94 seconds due to the fuse box fault Daniel is mid-repair on.
In the dark, Leo crosses to the fireplace, strikes Jake once with the poker, and returns to his position before the lights return.
Power returns. Jake is found dead by the fireplace.
In the panic afterward, Sam quietly removes his hidden device from under the table and hides it in Priya's bag.
Police arrive; the group's statements are first taken.

SUS1.initial_interview: Calm, cooperative, expresses genuine grief. Sticks to a simple account: seated across the table, ran to Jake when the lights returned.

solution.role_cover: Devoted friend, model fiance, promising medical student, nothing about him invites suspicion
solution.true_identity: The one member of the friend group with the most to lose from Jake's planned confession
solution.true_motive: To prevent the three-year-old hit-and-run cover-up from being exposed, which would end his medical career, his engagement, and his family's standing
solution.how_it_happened: During the 94-second blackout caused by an unrelated, genuine electrical fault, Leo crossed the dark room to the fireplace, struck Jake once with the iron poker, and returned to his position before the lights came back, relying on the panic and darkness to cover both the act and the sound.
solution.why_no_direct_evidence_exists_for_this_s: The blackout was real and unplanned by Leo, giving him a genuine, unpredictable window rather than a staged one, and the seance's own manufactured fear (from Sam's separate prank) absorbed all initial suspicion before anyone considered a mundane, personal motive.
key_proof_chain: EV013 - Text proving Leo specifically knew about the confession two days prior
EV007 - CCTV proving Leo's unexplained early presence near the manor
EV032 - Leo's own inconsistent statement about his movement during the blackout
EV036 - The exact 94-second blackout window from the fuse box log
EV051 - Final fingerprint match on the poker
EV052 - The full reconstructed timeline tying all of the above into one sequence
solution.how_case_is_broken: The case is solved by first working through and clearing the two decoy mysteries (Sam's prank, Priya's frame-up), then connecting Leo's specific, personal motive (via the hit-and-run cover-up) to his unexplained early presence and the narrow physical window the blackout provided, culminating in the fingerprint match and reconstructed timeline.

hidden_truth.full_narrative: Three years ago, five inseparable college friends made one irreversible mistake: driving home drunk from a party, they struck and killed Elena Reyes, panicked, and made a pact of silence that all five have carried since. The guilt affected each of them differently, Priya turned it into years of anonymous financial atonement; Mia buried it beneath a carefully built new life; Sam distracted himself with humor and hobbies; Leo compartmentalized it entirely, building a future that depended on the past staying buried; and Jake, unable to carry it any longer, quietly began therapy and eventually decided to confess to police, reaching out privately first to make peace with Elena's family. He told only Leo directly, out of a mix of guilt and respect for how much it would cost him. During what was meant to be a lighthearted last reunion, Sam's harmless prank, rigging the Ouija board to spell a word and spook everyone, created an atmosphere of genuine dread completely by coincidence, moments before a real, unrelated electrical fault plunged the manor into darkness. In that narrow, genuinely unplanned window, Leo made an impulsive, desperate choice: he crossed the room and killed Jake, then returned to his position before the lights came back, letting the fear of something supernatural or someone dangerous in the dark become the story everyone else reached for first. Sam's panicked decision to hide his prank device in Priya's bag afterward very nearly sent the investigation down an entirely wrong path, and the emergence of the old hit-and-run very nearly implicated Daniel Reyes, the one person with an obvious motive who had, in fact, already made peace with the past days before the murder. The truth was never in the seance at all, it was in a car, three years earlier, and in exactly how much one person stood to lose from it finally coming out.

why_every_suspect_lied.Leo Bennett: Lied about his early visit to the manor and his exact movements during the blackout to conceal the murder itself.
why_every_suspect_lied.Sam Ostrowski: Lied about the seance device entirely, then compounded it by planting it in Priya's bag, purely to avoid being blamed for planning a murder he had no part in.
why_every_suspect_lied.Priya Anand: Withheld her financial records and her role in the old cover-up out of shame and fear for her career, not out of involvement in the murder.
why_every_suspect_lied.Mia Torres: Downplayed her argument with Jake out of embarrassment and fear the old secret would surface, not out of guilt over his death.
why_every_suspect_lied.Daniel Reyes: Didn't lie so much as withhold context, he saw no reason to volunteer his family history unless asked directly.

hidden_truth.why_every_red_herring_exists: Sam's prank device created the illusion of a planned, malicious seance; its discovery in Priya's bag created a second, false suspect; Mia's argument with Jake created a third, emotionally convincing motive; and Daniel's family connection to an old tragedy created the most obvious revenge motive of all, each one real, each one investigated fairly, each one ultimately unconnected to the actual killer.
